_comment: Parity fixture for the M6-05 TUI permission dialogs. Lock the LingXi-locked button labels (which deliberately diverge from claude-code's React Select labels — claude-code uses 'Yes' / 'Yes, and don't ask again for X commands in Y' / 'No'; LingXi uses '[1] Allow Once / [2] Allow Always / [N] Deny' to surface the numeric-key affordance) AND the keymap, so any future label rename gets caught in CI.

tool_use_confirm.header_template: Claude needs your permission to use {tool_name}

exit_plan_mode.header: LingXi needs your approval for the plan

bypass_permissions.title: WARNING: LingXi running in Bypass Permissions mode
bypass_permissions.body_1:
In Bypass Permissions mode, LingXi will not ask for your approval before running potentially dangerous commands.
This mode should only be used in a sandboxed container/VM that has restricted internet access and can easily be restored if damaged.
bypass_permissions.body_2: By proceeding, you accept all responsibility for actions taken while running in Bypass Permissions mode.

focus_trap._comment: When a dialog is open, key events do NOT reach PromptInput. This is enforced by events::keymap::handle_key.
